feature_descriptions.ss02: allow ·I·Tea to join at the Short height
feature_descriptions.ss03: let x-height exiters join ·Tea: full-size when a baseline-join follows, else the half ·Tea
feature_descriptions.ss04: allow ·It to join at baseline after ·Day and before ·Low
feature_descriptions.ss05: allow ·Et·Tea·… double baseline joins again (older, manual-style behavior)
feature_descriptions.ss06: use gapped ·Owe (doesn’t connect at the top)
feature_descriptions.ss07: allow ·Owe·Day to join at the x-height again
feature_descriptions.ss10: suppress all joins for the wrapped letter(s)

machine_approved.method: Shaped with uharfbuzz in both fixture fonts under every config in the unit's set; outlines decomposed, translated, sorted, and compared.

classes.title: Join dropped
classes.summary: Letters the old font joined stand apart, for example `·At | ·It` and `·It | ·Et`, where the old font drew `·At ~x~ ·It` and `·It ~x~ ·Et`.
classes.why: No junction gains a join, and some junction goes from a join to a break; the leftmost such junction names the pair.

classes.title: ss03 keeps the ·Tea+Oy ligature
classes.summary: With ss03 on, ·Tea·Oy still forms ·Tea+Oy, so `·May ~x~ ·Tea.half | ·Oy` becomes `·May | ·Tea+Oy`.
classes.note: The 2 units left also gain a join before ·May (`·Way ~b~ ·May`, `·He ~b~ ·May`), which no ruling covers.
classes.why:
With ss03 on, the rebuild forms ·Tea+Oy where the old font drew half-·Tea joined to the letter before it and left ·Oy apart.
You approved it as a whole: the old font's split is never preferred unless the letter before is ·Out.

split-by-space-or-zwnj.title: Split by a space or ZWNJ
split-by-space-or-zwnj.summary: A space or ZWNJ ends the word, so each piece draws exactly as it does standing alone.
split-by-space-or-zwnj.why: The word-boundary rule decides it: a space or ZWNJ splits the run, and the split-buffer check confirms each piece shapes as it does alone.

ss03-tea-oy-ligature-kept.title: ss03 keeps the ·Tea+Oy ligature
ss03-tea-oy-ligature-kept.summary: With ss03 on, ·Tea·Oy still forms ·Tea+Oy, so `·May ~x~ ·Tea.half | ·Oy` becomes `·May | ·Tea+Oy`.
ss03-tea-oy-ligature-kept.why:
With ss03 on, the rebuild forms ·Tea+Oy where the old font drew half-·Tea joined to the letter before it and left ·Oy apart.
You approved it as a whole: the old font's split is never preferred unless the letter before is ·Out.

identical-unused-join-name.title: Looks identical: unused join in the old names
identical-unused-join-name.summary: A glyph the old font named for a join that never formed draws exactly as in the old font; only glyph names differ.
identical-unused-join-name.why: The old font named a glyph for a join that never formed, and the rebuild names it plainly. The ink is the same.

identical-see-out-fusion.title: Looks identical: ·See·Out fusion
identical-see-out-fusion.summary: The ·See·Out fusion draws exactly as in the old font; only glyph names differ.
identical-see-out-fusion.why:
The baseline ·See·Out fusion puts the junction's pull-back on the other side from the old font.
The renaming itself redraws no ink, which is what `ink_identical: true` states.
